source.title: Analyzing Visual Representations in Embodied Navigation Tasks
source.authors: Erik Wijmans; Julian Straub; Dhruv Batra; Irfan Essa; Judy Hoffman; Ari S. Morcos

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures representational similarity with PWCCA and compares models trained on different task splits against same-task models. This is a conceptual test of convergence across random initializations, using a measure and setting different from the original convergence-learning work.
record.gate_note: The paper reports layerwise PWCCA comparisons and transfer-learning outcomes. The PWCCA comparisons bear on V3; the transfer results do not test whether representations are mapped or aligned by one of the methods in V4. The text does not test convergence with scale, cross-modal alignment, universal features, or sensitivity to alternative similarity measures. Exact curve values are not stated in the text.
record.test_reason: The study trains same-architecture navigation agents from different seeds and compares their visual encoders layerwise with PWCCA. Its same-task, seed-to-seed comparisons, the baseline for the cross-task test, bear on V3 in a new setting (deep RL embodied navigation). The main question, task dependence, fits no version directly.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that slight task differences (target-object splits, environment layouts) have no measurable effect on visual representations beyond seed variation, for SqueezeNet and ResNet. Such representations transfer with better sample efficiency. They caveat that the tasks are quite similar, and suggest that coverage of the visual space is a key ingredient.
record.recipe_differences: Uses layerwise PWCCA to compare independently trained reinforcement-learning agents across related task and environment splits, grounding cross-task distances against same-task distances.

fits_no_version.finding: Networks trained on disjoint target-object splits or disjoint environment layouts are no more different (PWCCA) than networks differing only by seed.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Slightly different tasks or data in the same visual domain induce representations as similar as seed replicates.

fits_no_version.finding: A frozen visual encoder trained on one split supports more sample-efficient learning of another split.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Task-agnostic visual representations in embodied navigation transfer across related tasks.

record.problems: The authors state that the tasks examined are quite similar. Exact PWCCA and transfer-curve values are not given in the text, and several results are presented graphically. The study uses PWCCA rather than comparing multiple similarity measures.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows omitted. Layerwise numerical values and individual plotted curves are not reproduced because exact values are not stated in the text; the aggregate qualitative findings are recorded.

untested.parts: No scale or capability sweep; there are two small encoders of similar size.
No unit-level or feature-level matching; whole-layer PWCCA only. Seed similarity is not quantified in the text.
No cross-model mapping or stitching. Frozen-encoder transfer reuses one model rather than mapping between two.
Single metric (PWCCA) and single input set; no metric or OOD comparison.
No plateau or causal analysis of alignment.

missing.what: Statement that, in ResNet35, the distance induced by random seeds decreases between down-sampling layers, suggesting residual connections increase similarity.
Absolute seed-to-seed (A, B) PWCCA distance levels per layer, needed to judge the degree of cross-seed convergence.
Average ΔDpwcca across environments (A-B minus same-task), plotted within about ±0.04.

record.verdict_notes: This is not an original source for any version. Linking R1–R6 to V3 is indirect: the paper uses seed variation as a baseline rather than testing seed convergence itself. Researchers may prefer to treat the main result as fits_no_version only.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep over model scale or capability, and no comparison across different architectures, objectives, or data regimes aimed at convergence with scale.
No paired image-caption or other vision-language comparison.
The study compares whole-layer representations with PWCCA, not individual units or explicitly identified shared features. Its main comparisons use closely related tasks and environments.
The study transfers frozen visual encoders to new tasks, but does not test a map between two models' representations, stitching, relative representations, or alignment without paired data.
No interpretable neurons, SAE features, or circuits are identified or compared.
The study uses PWCCA and does not compare similarity metrics, settings such as neighbour count, or in-distribution versus out-of-distribution inputs.
The study does not test whether alignment plateaus or whether shared data or objectives cause alignment rather than a common model of reality.

rows.subject: SqueezeNet1.2 ObjectNav agents
rows.size_stated: ∼1.7 × 10^6 total agent parameters; ∼80% are in the visual encoder
rows.operation_detail: Compared layerwise PWCCA distances for agents trained on the same versus disjoint random target-object splits.

conditions.value: three random choices of disjoint, equally sized target-object sets A and B

rows.baseline: Distances between models trained on the same task (A-A and B-B)
rows.value: A-B distances were described as similar to same-task distances; no measurable effect of the target split on visual representations.
rows.uncertainty: 95% confidence interval by empirical bootstrapping is shown; numeric interval not stated.
rows.note: The result is reported across layerwise comparisons; the text gives the qualitative comparison but not exact PWCCA values.
rows.check: The value records the A-B vs A/A-B comparison (task dependence). The V3-relevant evidence is the seed-to-seed A and B curves, which are only plotted (axis about 0–0.4 Dpwcca), so the 'observed' state rests on figure reading, not stated numbers.

rows.value: The authors report the same trend as for SqueezeNet: the target split did not measurably affect the learned visual representation.
rows.note: The text describes the trend; exact values are only plotted.
rows.check: Same issue as R1. Also omits the stated finding that seed-induced distance decreases between down-sampling layers in ResNet35.

relationships.condition: SqueezeNet1.2 and ResNet35 visual encoders of PPO navigation agents (ObjectNav, PointNav), Replica environments
relationships.reason: Seed-to-seed PWCCA distances are low but nonzero across layers (plotted roughly 0.1–0.3), consistent with shared subspaces (R1–R6). This rests on figure axes, not stated numbers.
relationships.display_finding: Cross-seed PWCCA distances remained low but nonzero across layers, visually estimated at roughly 0.1–0.3.
